root_cause.text: In `drivers/power/supply/pm8916_bms_vm.c`, `pm8916_bms_vm_battery_probe()` requested the IRQ with `devm_request_threaded_irq()` before registering the `power_supply`, creating a lifetime/order mismatch where the IRQ handler could run with `bat->psy` uninitialized during probe or freed during devm teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `platform_get_irq_byname()` and `devm_request_threaded_irq()` block from before power-supply setup to after it, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that requesting the IRQ first causes reverse-order devm cleanup to free/unregister the `power_supply` before the IRQ is unregistered, allowing `power_supply_changed()` to be called on a freed or uninitialized handle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop requesting the unused FIFO IRQ during probe so the driver no longer depends on that interrupt and avoids probe failures related to it.
intent_record.what: The probe function removes the retrieval of the "fifo" IRQ via platform_get_irq_byname(), deletes the negative-IRQ error return, and deletes the devm_request_threaded_irq() call that registered pm8916_bms_vm_fifo_update_done_irq as a threaded interrupt handler.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver no longer looks up or requests the "fifo" interrupt during probe, so probe will not fail due to a missing or unrequestable FIFO IRQ and the FIFO update-done interrupt handler will no longer be installed or invoked.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the FIFO interrupt during probe and fail initialization if it cannot be set up so the battery driver can handle FIFO update completion events correctly.
intent_record.what: The probe function was modified to retrieve an IRQ named "fifo" using platform_get_irq_byname(), return immediately if that lookup fails, and register a threaded interrupt handler with devm_request_threaded_irq() using pm8916_bms_vm_fifo_update_done_irq, IRQF_ONESHOT, the name "pm8916_vm_bms", and the battery driver data pointer before calling platform_set_drvdata().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver now acquires and enables handling for the FIFO-related hardware interrupt during probe, so the pm8916_bms_vm_fifo_update_done_irq handler will be invoked when that interrupt fires. If the IRQ is unavailable or registration fails, probe now aborts instead of continuing without interrupt support.

Register the FIFO interrupt during probe and fail initialization if it cannot be set up so the battery driver can handle FIFO update completion events correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is an IRQ/power_supply lifetime ordering bug for the battery IRQ path, where the handler could access bat->psy before registration or after teardown. This change only removes an unused FIFO IRQ request to avoid dependency/probe failures, not the ordering mismatch involving bat->psy.

The change is about adding/setup of a FIFO interrupt for functionality and probe failure handling, not about fixing the ordering/lifetime mismatch between IRQ registration and power_supply registration or preventing the handler from accessing an uninitialized/freed bat->psy.

candidates.rationale: This is the operation that installs the IRQ handler too early in probe. Because it happens before power_supply registration, the handler can run while bat->psy is still uninitialized, and during devm teardown the IRQ lifetime can outlive the power_supply lifetime ordering.
This is the continuation of the IRQ registration call that binds the threaded handler to bat during probe, directly creating the lifetime/order mismatch described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement begins the IRQ registration during probe. Registering the threaded IRQ before the power_supply is registered creates the ordering/lifetime mismatch: the handler can run before bat->psy is initialized, and devm-managed IRQ teardown can race with or outlive the power_supply lifetime.

This is the completion of the same devm_request_threaded_irq() call that binds the IRQ handler to bat. Together with the preceding line, it installs the handler too early in probe and causes the vulnerable lifetime/order mismatch described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The probe function clearly shows the problematic ordering. It requests the IRQ early with `devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, pm8916_bms_vm_fifo_update_done_irq, IRQF_ONESHOT, "pm8916_vm_bms", bat);` before the power supply is registered. Later, only after multiple register operations, it does `bat->battery = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &pm8916_bms_vm_battery_psy_desc, &psy_cfg);`. The IRQ handler `pm8916_bms_vm_fifo_update_done_irq()` calls `power_supply_changed(bat->battery);`, so if the IRQ fires before registration, `bat->battery` is still uninitialized/NULL. Because both resources are devm-managed and the IRQ was registered first, teardown can also invoke the same lifetime/order mismatch described in the root cause, with the IRQ potentially still runnable after the power supply has been released. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix (registering the power_supply before requesting the IRQ / otherwise ensuring correct lifetime ordering) is not present in this version.

It requests the IRQ early with `devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, pm8916_bms_vm_fifo_update_done_irq, IRQF_ONESHOT, "pm8916_vm_bms", bat);` before the power_supply is registered later with `bat->battery = devm_power_supply_register(...)`.
